data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resilience to correlated failure is not a property of the network topology (centralized vs. decentralized) but a property of the 'Evolutionary Divergence' of the system's state-space.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services converge on a single dominant framework or library (e.g., all using the same version of an OpenSSL wrapper).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The environment imposes a singular, overwhelming stressor that exceeds the capacity of all divergent implementations (e.g., a global BGP routing collapse).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Correlated failures occur when diverse entities share a common 'blind spot' in their state-space. A large service with redundancy often shares a single evolutionary trajectory (same codebase, same CI/CD pipeline, same operator logic), creating a 'monoculture of failure'. A decentralized network, by evolving under different environmental pressures and operator incentives, develops 'Orthogonal Failure Modes'. Resilience is thus proportional to the degree of divergent evolution in implementation, not the number of nodes or the lack of a central authority.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
